request.query: How many days or weeks did you wait for a Vero (Tax Administration) appointment for Personal identity code from a Vero tax office in Oulu, and how long until it was done?
request.objective: Forum posts, Reddit threads, blogs and university guides from people who did "Personal identity code from a Vero tax office" (Vero (Tax Administration)) in Oulu, Finland: how long they waited for an appointment or for the result, and appointment availability.

results.title: Finnish personal identity code: get a henkilötunnus | Hello Expat
results.author: The Hello Expat editorial team
highlights:
## How do you register at the DVV step by step?

1. Fill in the online form. It is the "Registration Information of a Foreigner" form. You do not need electronic identification, and a paper form exists.
2. Book an appointment. The DVV requires a visit in person. You must come within one month of submitting the form, and children come too.
3. Bring your documents: a valid passport or EU/EEA identity card, your Migri EU registration certificate or residence document, proof of work or studies (a contract or a school certificate), and, if you claim family ties, civil-status certificates, legalised and translated where required.
4. State your language. Tell the DVV whether you want service in Finnish or Swedish.
5. Ask for a municipality of residence on the same form if you stay at least a year.
6. Wait. The identity code is issued 2 to 3 weeks after the visit if you work or study, and 3 to 4 weeks otherwise.

The same form can be used for children under 18 who arrive with you. International House centres in Helsinki, Joensuu, Oulu, Rauma, Tampere and Turku (and International Pointti in Kemi) pull several agencies under one roof, and the DVV is present in them. They are worth knowing if your first appointment needs help in English.

...

## How do you get a Finnish tax card?

Once you have your henkilötunnus, you apply to Verohallinto (Vero, the Tax Administration) for a verokortti, the tax card. Vero says that applying for one requires a Finnish personal identity code. If a visit is needed, Vero gives you an appointment. Processing normally takes one to three working days when all information is available.

...

Give a copy to your employer.

...

Ask Vero or the DVV for the code in the same visit as your tax card application. Some tax offices in large cities can issue an identity code at the same time. If you start anyway without a tax card, your employer withholds 60 per cent of your salary. It comes back later through the tax return, but your cash flow suffers in the meantime.

...

How long does it take to get a henkilötunnus?+

The DVV says 2 to 3 weeks if you came to work or study and 3 to 4 weeks in other cases. The count starts on the day of your visit to the DVV.

results.title: Streamlined services for issuing personal identity codes and municipality of residence for foreign citizens - Finnish Government
results.author: Digi- ja väestötietovirasto
highlights:
The Digital and Population Data Services Agency took action last year in order to streamline the registration of foreigners. You can now get your personal identity code when visiting the agency in 12 locations. The updated website and instructional videos will guide customers to use services that match their situation.

The registration of foreigners' personal data has accelerated as the Digital and Population Data Services Agency has improved its practices and systems. You can now apply for a personal identity code and municipality of residence online, which speeds up processing and improves the accuracy of the data. After filling in the online form, the customer must still usually visit the agency in order to verify their identity.

...

## Customers can receive their personal identity code in connection to a visit 

A few service locations of the Digital and Population Data Services Agency tested the practice first and started issuing a personal identity code during a personal visit, and as their experiences were positive, the practice was adopted permanently. At the moment, persons who have booked an appointment and completed an online form may receive their personal identity code in 12 locations: Helsinki, Joensuu, Jyväskylä, Kuopio, Lahti, Lappeenranta, Oulu, Pori, Rovaniemi, Tampere, Turku and Vaasa. 

To receive their personal identity code during the visit, the customer must first submit their data to the Digital and Population Data Services Agency using an online form and book an appointment online. They must also meet the requirements for obtaining a personal identity code. However, a personal identity code cannot always be issued during a visit if the matter requires further clarification. 

The online form for obtaining a personal identity code is available to all foreigners, and it does not require strong identification. You can use the same form to request a municipality of residence if you are intending to stay in Finland for more than one year. The conditions for obtaining a personal identity code and municipality of residence are examined individually for each customer.

...

Having a Finnish personal identity code makes many everyday matters possible, such as dealing with the authorities, opening a bank account and receiving wages. In addition to the Digital and Population Data Services Agency, a foreigner may in certain situations receive a personal identity code from the Tax Administration or the Finnish Immigration Service.

results.title: How Long Does It Take to Get a Personal Identity Code in Finland? - Finland Handbook
results.author: Finland Handbook Editorial Team
highlights:
However, for EU citizens or those who didn't receive a code with their permit, the process involves a visit to the DVV. In 2026, the standard processing time for a Personal Identity Code at the DVV is generally 1 to 3 weeks after your appointment. The real challenge is often securing the appointment itself. In major cities like Helsinki, Espoo, or Tampere, the "wait for the wait" can be significant. You might find that the first available slot for identity verification is three weeks away, and only after that does the 1–3 week processing clock begin. Understanding Getting Your Personal Identity Code: The Key to Finnish Healthcare is essential here, as this code is the bedrock of your entire administrative life in Finland.

| Application Path | Typical Processing Time | Key Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Residence Permit (Migri) | Linked to permit (1–6 months) | Applied for abroad or at Migri |
| EU Citizen (DVV) | 1–3 weeks after appointment | Valid passport & proof of work/study |
| Nordic Citizen (DVV) | 1 week | Personal appearance at DVV |
| Temporary Worker (Short-term) | 1–2 weeks | Finnish employer's confirmation |

results.title: DVV Registration Finland: Get Your Henkilötunnus (2026) | NordicExpat
results.author: Bikram Nath
highlights:
Who needs it

Foreign citizens moving to Finland on work, study, family or

...

Cost

Free — no fee for the henkilötunnus or municipality decision

How long

2–3 weeks (work/study) or 3–4 weeks (other cases), from your in-person visit

Where to apply

Online form at dvv.fi, then in person at a DVV service point (Helsinki, Tampere, Turku, Oulu)

...

DVV registration in Finland is how a foreigner enters the Population Information System and receives a henkilötunnus (personal identity code) that banks, the tax office and Kela rely on. You register with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency by submitting an online registration form, then attending one in-person appointment within a month. It is free and takes roughly two to four weeks.

...

Register with DVV in two stages: submit the free online foreigner registration form at dvv.fi/en/foreigner-registration (no authentication needed), then visit a DVV service point in person within 1 month with your passport, residence permit or EU registration certificate, and proof of work or study. Processing then takes 2–3 weeks for work and study cases, 3–4 weeks otherwise. There is no fee — the registration and your henkilötunnus (personal identity code) are completely free.

...

The registration is for people who are genuinely settling in for a meaningful period, not for tourists or very short visits. If you need the code for tax reasons when you start working in Finland, a tax office can also issue a personal identity code — but that alone does not give you a municipality of residence. (For the mechanics of the code itself, see our guide to the Finnish personal identity code.)

...

### Step 2 — Book an in-person appointment within one month

After the form, you must visit a DVV service point in person, and you must do so within one month of submitting. The in-person step is non-negotiable — it is where DVV verifies your identity against your documents. Appointments at the busy Helsinki-area locations can fill up, so book as early as you can rather than leaving it to the end of the one-month window.

...

### Step 4 — Wait for processing

Processing time, according to DVV, is roughly 2–3 weeks for work and study registrations and 3–4 weeks for other cases, counted from your visit date. At the end you receive your personal identity code, and DVV separately decides your municipality of residence.

...

DVV operates service points across Finland — major cities including Helsinki, Tampere, Turku, and Oulu have offices, and there are around a dozen physical locations nationally. You can also reach DVV by telephone on +358 295 536 320 (Mon–Fri 9–15) and through secure email for questions about your case.

...

## A Realistic Timeline for Your First Month

Putting it together, a typical sequence for a new arrival looks like this:

1. Before or on arrival — settle your residence basis with Migri (permit for non-EU; right-of-residence registration for EU citizens staying over three months).
2. First days — submit the DVV foreigner registration form online and book the in-person appointment.
3. Within the first month — attend the DVV appointment with your documents; this is also a good moment to use International House Helsinki if you are in the capital region.
4. Weeks two to four — DVV processes the registration (2–3 weeks for work/study, 3–4 weeks otherwise) and assigns your personal identity code and, where eligible, your municipality of residence.
5. Once you have the henkilötunnus — open a Finnish bank account, order a tax card from Vero, and register with Kela.
6. Whenever you move permanently or for over 3 months — file a notification of move within one week.

The order matters because each step depends on the one before it. The single most useful thing you can do is start the DVV form early and book the appointment immediately, since the in-person slot is usually the bottleneck. Everything downstream — banking, tax, healthcare — is waiting on the code DVV gives you at the end.

results.title: Personal identity code in Finland - Herizon
highlights:
As a foreign citizen you get a Finnish personal identity code (henkilötunnus) by registering with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV): you submit its form, then visit a DVV service point in person within one month. DVV's registration page states: "Everyone who requests a personal identity code must visit in person within 1 month of submitting the form, including children." Registration is free of charge, and DVV processes a request based on work or study in 2 to 3 weeks counted from the day of your visit. The code alone does not give you a municipality of residence (kotikunta), which is a separate decision with its own conditions.

...

1. Fill in the form. DVV's online form "does not require authentication". One parent can request a code on the same form for a child under 18 who moves to Finland at the same time.
2. Book the visit at once. Book your appointment through DVV's registration page. The one-month clock starts on the day you submit the form, so book in the same sitting.
3. Bring the documents. DVV lists a valid passport or an official photo ID card (for EU, EEA and certain other nationals); a residence permit card or other proof that you reside legally in Finland; the EU registration certificate if you have one; and proof of work or studies, "for example, a certificate of student status or an employment contract".

...

Add family documents if needed. If you also register a marriage or parenthood, bring the completed forms and the certificates, legalised and translated where DVV's rules require it.

DVV's registration page sets these processing times and fee:

| Request | Processing time | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code request based on work or study | 2 to 3 weeks from the visit | Free |
| Code request on other grounds | 3 to 4 weeks from the visit | Free |

...

Take a non-EU specialist with a continuous (A) residence permit. The DVV form goes in, the appointment is booked within the month, and the passport, permit card and employment contract go to the visit. DVV states the code takes 2 to 3 weeks from the visit for work-based requests. A municipality of residence may be granted at the same time if DVV's conditions are met, which an A permit satisfies when the person also intends to stay at least a year. The tax card can be applied for once the code exists, as the Tax Administration requires it.

...

### How long does it take to get a personal identity code in Finland?

DVV's registration page gives 2 to 3 weeks for a request based on work or study and 3 to 4 weeks for other grounds. The clock starts on the day of your in-person visit, so a late appointment delays the code.
